campaign.days: Days 4 to 20: the Long Winter and Fimbulwinter.
request.freyja: Freyja wants some of Odin's worthy dead for her meadow. "He has so many. He won't count."
request.odin: Odin wants Freyja's chosen for his hall. The best of the fallen are his by right, he says, whatever she has decided they wear.
request.hel: Hel wants some of Odin's warriors for her legion. Ragnarök will need them on her side of it, she says, more than he will.
request.clerk: The clerk wants heathens bound for Hel, for the water. He has brought the forms.
favour.odin: the sun holds a minute longer at the gate
favour.freyja: your first question of the day costs no sun
favour.hel: no one at home falls sick by chance, and the sick hold out a night longer without medicine
favour.freyja.more: your second question of the day costs no sun either
favour.hel.more: the sick hold out another night
favour.clerk.more: the rest of your fines are waived
favour.loki: a ring a nail, ten rings for each soul you send on with its nails uncut
rank.second.text: Odin's steward has noticed your clean days. The gate would trust you with more of the dead, and Odin would take his share of what you're paid.
rank.first.text: Few are offered this. The gate would send you more of the dead than it sends anyone, and forgive you nothing, and Odin would take his share.
decree.d4: Freyja has claimed her share of the slain. Each day she names a whim; the worthy who match it go to Fólkvangr.
decree.d5: A sea battle. The drowned belong to Rán, whatever they tell you.
whim.amber: Freyja claims whoever wears amber today.
shop.sundial.text: Skögul teaches you to read the sun. Each shift gets 30 more seconds.
decree.d6: Odin decrees: outlaws and oathbreakers named in the registry go to Hel, whatever else is true. Search the registry when you have cause to.
rule.outlaw: Outlaws and oathbreakers named in the registry go to Hel. Stamp HEL.
law.registry: If the registry names this soul (same name, same hair), they are an outlaw.
law.unregistered: If the registry has nobody by that name, or only someone else who shares it, they are not.
cue.brokenRing: A broken oath-ring on a thong
tm.oath.kept.1: I never broke an oath in my life. Ask anyone.
tm.oath.kept.2: My word is iron. Every oath I swore, I kept.
tm.oath.kept.3: I kept faith with my jarl to the end.
q.oath.confess.1: …All right. I swore on the ring and ran when it counted. The clerks wrote it down, didn't they.
q.oath.confess.2: It was one oath. One. And the jarl deserved it.
q.oath.excuse.1: Oaths are complicated. I'd rather not say more.
rv.huginn.outlaw: Huginn saw {name} break an oath sworn on the ring.
case.geir.knows: You know me. I sat at your father's table every winter.
case.geir.plea: Whatever the clerks wrote down, it was a long time ago.
decree.d7: Odin decrees: only a warrior's own weapon counts. Whoever fell with a borrowed blade goes to Hel. You may use the rune-lens.
decree.d8: Odin decrees, against Naglfar: clip every soul's untrimmed nails before you send it on, whatever its stamp.
rule.borrowed: A soul who fell holding someone else's weapon goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
law.ownBlade: If the owner's runes name the soul ("…á mik", "…owns me"), the weapon is theirs.
law.borrowedBlade: If the owner's runes name someone else, the weapon was borrowed or taken.
law.copyUlfberht: A copy puts the cross at the end: +VLFBERHT+.
cue.wrongGrip: The grip is wrapped for a bigger hand
proc.clip: Clip untrimmed nails before sending a soul on (Naglfar decree).
obs.inscription.own: Owner's runes: "{name} á mik" ({name} owns me)
obs.inscription.other: Owner's runes: "{other} á mik" ({other} owns me)
tm.owner.self.1: This was my father's {weapon}, and his father's before him.
tm.owner.self.2: Nobody else has ever held this {weapon}. Nobody would dare.
tm.blade.ulfberht.1: My {weapon} was a true Ulfberht. You can read it on the blade.
tm.blade.ulfberht.2: A true Ulfberht {weapon}, bought in Hedeby for a year's silver.
q.owner.confess.1: …It was my brother's. Mine broke in the first rush. He wasn't using it; he was already dead.
q.blade.confess.1: The merchant swore it was real. I suppose he would.
decree.d11: Odin decrees: a soul's saga tally is evidence, unless it's forged. Under the rune-lens a forgery gives itself away (a rune from the old alphabet, a rune carved backwards, or a garbled carver's line). Ignore a forged tally entirely.
cue.freshCarving: A tally stick in the belt, its cuts fresh and pale
tell.elderRune: Under the lens: one rune, ᛗ, belongs to the old alphabet that carvers stopped using centuries ago.
tell.mirroredRune: Under the lens: one rune is carved backwards, the way a copier gets it wrong.
tell.brokenFormula: Under the lens: the carver's closing line is garbled ("reist mik" where it should say "reist rúnar").
tl.cause.sickness: Died of a fever in the winter.
tl.cause.oldAge: Died old, in bed, among grandchildren.
tl.fled.false: Never turned from the shield wall.
tl.fled.true: Turned and ran at the last.
tl.owner.self: Carried no weapon but their own.
tl.outlaw.false: Kept every oath sworn on the ring.
q.tally.confess.1: …I paid a carver in Ribe. Everybody does it. Well. Everybody who can afford it.
q.tally.confess.2: My brother carved it. He meant well. He can't spell either.
q.tally.excuse.1: I can't read. I just carried the stick they gave me.
decree.d10: Odin decrees, with the clerk of the White Christ reading over his shoulder: the baptized belong to the clerk. Stamp TRANSFER. The prime-signed, who took the sign of the cross but never the water, are still ours.
decree.d12: Odin decrees: Loki is walking among the dead in borrowed faces. The dwarf Brokkr once sewed his lips shut, and the scars never faded. Whoever bears them, stamp DETAIN.
rule.transfer: The baptized belong to the clerk of the White Christ. Stamp TRANSFER.
rule.detain: Loki, in whatever face he wears, is held for Odin. Stamp DETAIN.
law.cross: A cross at the neck means they took the water: baptized.
law.primeSigned: A hammer and a cross on one cord means prime-signed: the sign of the cross, never the water. Still ours.
law.hammer: Thor's hammer at the neck means they never took the water.
law.stitchedLips: Stitch scars across the lips mean Loki.
law.plainLips: Lips without scars mean it isn't Loki.
obs.amulet.hammerAndCross: A hammer and a cross on one cord
obs.lipScars.stitched: Small stitch scars across the lips
tm.creed.heathen.1: I kept to the old gods. Never took the water.
tm.creed.heathen.2: Thor's, born and buried. Put that on your slate.
tm.creed.baptized.1: I was washed in the White Christ's water at Hedeby. It was very cold.
tm.creed.baptized.2: I'm a Christian, me. Baptized and everything. Is the clerk's hall warm?
tm.creed.primeSigned.1: I took the sign of the cross to trade in York. Nobody put me in any water.
tm.guise.1: Just a plain {gender, select, f {woman} other {man}}, me. Nothing up my sleeves.
tm.guise.2: Honest as the day is long. And the days are getting long, aren't they?
q.creed.hid.confess.1: ...All right, I was washed. My mother-in-law made me. Don't tell Odin.
q.creed.claimed.confess.1: The hammer? A gift. A joke. ...Fine. I never saw a priest in my life.
q.creed.excuse.1: It's complicated. There was a river, and some singing, and I may have fallen in.
q.guise.deflect.1: Ask me something harder. You know you want to.
q.guise.deflect.2: What a clever question. Clever enough to get you into trouble. Next.
rv.huginn.baptized: Huginn: Saw this one dunked in a river by a man in a long robe. Twice, to be sure.
rv.huginn.primeSigned: Huginn: Took the sign of the cross at a market. Never the water. Kept the hammer too.
case.loki12.nails: You've been biting your nails. Don't. Somebody needs them.
case.loki12.again: We've met, haven't we? No. I'd remember a face like yours. I collect them.
ending.sliceEnd.title: The slice ends here
ending.sliceEnd.text: Twelve days at the gate. Loki walks among the dead, your brother is building a ship in the north, and Ragnarök is eight days away. The full game tells the rest.
rv.muninn.oathBroken: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Swore on the temple ring, then sold the jarl out for silver. I remember.
rv.muninn.oathKept: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Kept every oath. Every one. I remember because it was so rare.
rv.muninn.heathen: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Never went near the water. Sacrificed at Uppsala every ninth year.
rv.muninn.baptized: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Walked into a river after a man in a long robe. Came out a Christian.
rv.muninn.primeSigned: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Took the sign of the cross to trade at an English market. Never the water.
rv.muninn.ownWeapon: Muninn: That weapon was {name}'s own. It hung over the door at home. I remember.
rv.muninn.borrowedWeapon: Muninn: That weapon isn't {name}'s. Lifted from a dead man's hand.
decree.d9: A new decree. A jarl's sworn hearth-men who stood by him to the end go where he goes: judge the jarl, and you've judged them. And Odin's ring Draupnir drips tonight, eight rings for the chooser.
decree.d13: Odin decrees: both ravens will speak. Huginn saw how they died; Muninn remembers how they lived. They never lie, but they may seem to disagree. When they do, the Order of Judgment decides. And Muninn forgets more every day.
decree.d14: Hel sends word: her hall is full. Until she has room, those who died in their beds, of sickness or old age, go to the clerk, who says he has plenty. Everyone else Hel takes as before.
decree.d15: Odin decrees: he names his own claim each day, as Freyja does. When both of them want a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins and the soul goes to Valhalla. A blade with no maker's mark is plain: no Ulfberht.
rule.helFull: While Hel's hall is full, straw deaths (sickness, old age) that no earlier rule claims go to the clerk. Stamp TRANSFER.
rule.odinClaim: When Freyja's whim and Odin's claim both fit a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins. Stamp VALHALLA.
whim.odin.scarred: Odin claims the scarred today: two or more wounds in front.
whim.odin.ulfberht: Odin claims whoever carries a true Ulfberht today.
law.noMark: A blade with no maker's mark is a plain blade, not an Ulfberht.
decree.d16: Odin decrees: liars forfeit the halls of the worthy. A soul that would go to Valhalla or Fólkvangr but is caught in a lie, aloud or on a forged tally, goes to Hel. Catch every lie. Until you do, a soul is honest.
decree.d17: Odin decrees: those who died in their beds but were marked with a spear point before death are his, as he once marked himself. Look for the mark over the heart. Liars still forfeit it.
rule.liars: A soul the halls of the worthy would take, caught in a lie (aloud or on a forged tally), goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
rule.spearMark: A soul marked with a spear point before death is Odin's, even if they died in bed. Stamp VALHALLA.
obs.spearCut.true: A spear point's cut over the heart, made before death
q.blade.plain.confess.1: All right, it's a plain blade. A good plain blade. It killed people just the same.
p.hold.oath.1: Every oath I swore, I kept. Look me up, if you've a list.
p.hold.owner.1: It's mine. I carried it, I swung it, I died holding it.
p.hold.blade.1: A true Ulfberht. You can read the mark yourself.
p.hold.creed.heathen.1: Odin's own, born and burned. No water-priest ever touched me.
p.hold.creed.baptized.1: Baptized. Water, words, the lot. The priest was very thorough.
p.hold.guise.1: I'm exactly who I look like. Who else would I be?
decree.d18: No new decree. Draupnir drips tonight, for the last time. In the north they say Naglfar is nearly built.
decree.d19: No new decree. Every rule stands. Tomorrow the wolf is loose, so judge well tonight: every soul you send fights for someone.
decree.d18.noon: A raven lands on the desk with word from Odin: he has changed his claim since he stood at your table. From the soul after next, he wants others.
decree.d19.noon: A raven thumps down on the desk with word from Fólkvangr: Freyja has changed her mind, on the last day there is. From the soul after next, she wants others.
decree.d20: Ragnarök. Heimdall has blown the horn and the dead are coming all at once. Every rule stands. Judge as many as you can before the sun goes out.
shop.registryIndex.text: Skögul's tabs on the registry's edge. Searching it takes 2 seconds less.
shop.lensPolish.text: A cloth and a jar of fat for the rune-lens. Reading runes takes half the time.
shop.whetstone.text: Keeps the clippers keen. Clipping takes 2 seconds less.
shop.hornOfBrass.text: A louder question gets a quicker answer. Questioning costs 10 seconds instead of 20.
shop.waterClock.text: Measures the sun's last hour exactly, so none of it is wasted. Each shift gets 60 more seconds.
shop.goldFeather.text: A feather from her own cloak. It stirs at the faintest breath: the feather test takes 3 seconds.
shop.whaleLamp.text: Burns clean after dusk. Each shift gets 45 more seconds.
shop.runeTable.text: Every rune carved on one slate, by the lens. Reading runes takes 2 seconds.
shop.silverHorn.text: The dead answer before you've finished asking. Questioning costs 6 seconds.
ending.naglfar.title: Naglfar sails early
ending.naglfar.text:
You left the nails long, a few every day, and nobody at the gate said anything, because nobody at the gate counts nails except you.

The ship of dead men's nails leaves the north two days before the gods are ready. It moves the way a thing moves when it has been waiting a very long time. Loki is at the helm in his own face, and he waves.

He keeps his word, in his way. Your family is aboard: he chalked their names on the deck where the rail goes. So are you. There was always a place for you, he says. He would never have asked for their names without yours.

Behind you the queue is still coming up the path, and there is nobody at the table to stamp it. DRAFT.
ending.rebirth.title: The green earth
ending.rebirth.text:
You asked, when it would have been easier not to: Muninn, Móðguðr, Thorvald, Skögul. Every answer was a piece of the same song, and you put them together.

The horn blows. Your hosts hold where it matters, long enough. Then the fire comes anyway, as it was always going to, and the gods go into it, and the sea comes up over everything.

And then it goes down again. The earth comes up out of it green, and nobody has to sow it. Baldr walks out of Hel's hall with an old man a few steps behind him, talking about goats. Out of a wood in the hills come two people, and then a few more, blinking: your family, who waited on the dew. In the grass lie gold game pieces, where the old gods left them.

Someone will have to judge the dead in the new world. Nobody has asked you yet. You find you're hoping they will. DRAFT.
ending.smuggled.title: Smuggled home
ending.smuggled.text:
The ferryman is at the mouth of the fjord when the horn blows, exactly where he said and exactly on time. He counts your hundred rings without looking at them. Then he looks at your family, and counts them too.

While the gods look the other way, the grey boat takes them out past the skerries to a shore the wolf won't reach, because the wolf has never heard of it. Nobody has. That's what the rings were for.

You don't go with them. You go back up the path to the gate, where the queue is longer than it has ever been, and sit down, and pick up the stamp. Someone has to. DRAFT.
ending.transfer.title: The transfer
ending.transfer.text:
The clerk's contract was generous and full of small print, and you read every word of it, which the clerk says nobody has ever done.

When the horn blows, the transfer comes through. You are reassigned to a warmer room in another department, with a window, a pension and a table of your own. The forms are in triplicate. The clerk has already filled in two of them.

Your new department is very quiet. The dead who come to it have been judged somewhere else already, and only want to know where to sit. You tell them. Nobody asks you about wolves.

Some mornings you catch yourself listening for the horn. The clerk says that passes in time, and shows you the form for it. DRAFT.
ending.hel.title: Hel's steward
ending.hel.text:
Hel remembers who filled her hall when the gods wanted only heroes, and who said out loud, at the gate, that the quiet dead count.

Her gate held. Garm never got through. When the fire has burned itself out, Móðguðr comes up the path to your table, very tidy, and waits to be noticed.

"My lady would like a steward," she says. "For the quiet dead. The old, the sick, the ones who died in their beds. Someone who knows what they're worth."

So you go down, over the bridge roofed with gold, and it rings once for you. Hel's hall is long and dim and full, and nobody in it is shouting about glory. You find your grandfather on a bench by the fire, talking about goats to anyone who'll stay. You're good at this. You always were. DRAFT.
ending.freyja.title: Freyja's own
ending.freyja.text:
You gave Freyja the souls she asked for, whatever Odin's decrees said, and she noticed. Freyja always notices. She keeps a list.

At Ragnarök her field holds against the fire. The chosen of Fólkvangr stand where she put them and don't move, and when it's over the field is still there, and so is she.

She comes for you herself, in her cloak of feathers, and takes you in among the chosen, the way Valkyries were chosen once, before they did any choosing of their own. Nobody stamps anything in Fólkvangr. You sit in the long grass with the others, and when someone new comes across the field, you're the one who goes to meet them. DRAFT.
ending.odin.title: Chooser eternal
ending.odin.text:
Odin's hall was full and his host was strong, and the einherjar held the wolf longer than the seeress said they would. It isn't enough. It was never going to be. He falls to the wolf anyway, as foretold, with his one eye open.

Before he goes, he comes down to the gate in the grey hood and the wide hat, the one he thinks nobody knows him in. He stands at your table and looks at your stamps for a long time.

"There will be dead in the next world too," he says. "Somebody will have to choose."

He names you chooser for whatever comes after, and rides out. You're still at the table when the fire comes, holding the stamp, waiting for the first soul of the new world to come up the path. DRAFT.
ending.wolf.title: The wolf wins
ending.wolf.text:
Too few worthy dead, too many who ran, and the fronts went one by one. The wolf came through first, and the fire behind it. The gods fall quickly. It isn't how the songs tell it. The songs were made by people who expected to win.

From the gate you watch the fire come down the valley. The queue is still coming up the path, longer than ever, and it's your job to stamp them, so you do. Valhalla. Hel. Rán. The stamps still work. Nobody has told them.

When the smoke reaches the table, you put the stamp down face down, so it won't mark the wood. DRAFT.
ending.lastStand.title: The last stand
ending.lastStand.text:
Twenty days at the gate. The horn blows, and the host you chose rides out: the worthy and the unworthy, the ones who'll run and the ones who won't. Some fronts hold and some fall, and the gods fall too, as they always said they would.

You stay at the table. Someone has to stamp the ones who come up the path, and they keep coming all through the last day, with their wounds and their stories and their weapons in their hands, asking where they're meant to go.

You tell them. It's what you're for.

What comes after is not yours to judge. DRAFT.
arms.wolf.text: Ash shafts and new heads. The wolf is big; the spears are long.
arms.fire.text: Ox hides soaked in the fjord, for the field to hold against the fire.
arms.gate.text: The quiet dead fight better fed. Móðguðr will see it shared out.
arms.ship: Hooks and pitch for the shore
arms.ship.text: Grappling hooks and a pot of pitch for the drowned, for when the ship of nails comes in.
epi.refuge.wood: They went up into Hoddmímir's wood the night before the horn, with the goats and too much bread, and lived on the dew, as the song says. The song doesn't say what the wood gives back when the world doesn't end the way it should. Nobody has asked it.
epi.refuge.ferry: The ferryman was at the mouth of the fjord when the horn blew, on time to the moment, and asked for his hundred rings. You were short. He left without them, and they walked home along the shingle with their bundles.
epi.refuge.shipTurned: Loki kept their places. When the horn blew they were at the rail of his ship, the only passengers who had paid in names. The drowned turned it back at the shore, and it went north again with them aboard. Somewhere very dry, Loki says. He says they're well.
epi.refuge.ship: Loki kept their places. When the horn blew they were at the rail of his ship, the only passengers who had paid in names. At the shore he put them off first, before anything else came down the plank, which is more than he did for the gods.
epi.refuge.home: They were at home when the horn blew, with the fire banked high and the door barred, the way you told them. Whatever came had to knock.
epi.refuge.broke: You had their names rubbed off Loki's deck two nights before the horn, and there wasn't a night left to write another plan. They stayed at home and barred the door, and told each other it had been the plan all along.
epi.refuge.none: When the horn blew they were wherever they had chosen to be. Nobody told you where, and it seemed wrong to ask.
epi.ragna.crossed: Your mother crossed Móðguðr's bridge on the fourteenth morning and asked the way to her father's bench. She found it, and then found out who in the hall hadn't eaten.
epi.ragna.died: Your mother died at home before the end, of the winter. You never learned which door she went through. Wherever it was, she'll have asked who needed feeding.
epi.ragna.hill: Your mother's chest has been quiet since the morning on the hill. She tells anyone who'll listen that Eir held her hands, and that she has climbed worse for a goat.
epi.ragna.sick: Your mother was still coughing at the end. She said it was the smoke, and made everyone eat first.
epi.ragna.well: Your mother kept the fire, the goats and everyone's secrets to the end, and fed whoever came to the door, whichever side they were on.
epi.ulf.died: Ulf didn't see the end. He'd have told you not to make a fuss, and that the roof held through most of it.
epi.ulf.levy: Ulf came down from the pass with an arm that mended crooked. He doesn't talk about the cairn. He mends nets one-handed now, and says it's quicker.
epi.ulf.stayed: Ulf stayed home when the levy went, because you asked him to. He hasn't forgiven you. He's alive not to forgive you, and you'll take that.
epi.ulf.shipyard: Ulf built the rail of a ship in the north and never asked what the planks were made of. He's proud of the rail. It's very good work.
epi.ulf.debt: Ulf paid off his share of the smith's fine a ring at a time. He doesn't carve letters any more, not even his own name.
epi.ulf.home: Ulf mended nets and roofs to the end, counted every ring twice, and never once complained in a letter.
epi.asa.left: Asa went to your aunt in the valley before the end. She writes that the goats there are stupider, and draws you at the bottom of every letter, with wings.
epi.asa.sick: Asa's fever broke on the last night. The first thing she asked for was bread, and the second was you.
epi.asa.honest: Asa knows Grandfather is in Hel's hall, because your letters told the truth. She has decided he's keeping a bench for her, and has told everyone which one.
epi.asa.kind: Asa still thinks Grandfather rode to Valhalla with a horn in each hand. Nobody at home has the heart to tell her otherwise, and nobody at the gate will.
epi.asa.home: Asa asked one more time whether Grandfather had seen her. This time somebody said yes.
epi.tear: Asa wears Freyja's tear on a thong round her neck. She tells everyone it's a goddess's tear. Nobody believes her, and she doesn't mind.
epi.skogul.back: Skögul came back from the wolf's front with her spear in two pieces, sat on the end of your table and asked what there was to eat.
epi.skogul.ship: Skögul watched the ship go from the end of your table. She didn't wave, but she stopped eating, which from her is more.
epi.skogul.fell: Skögul rode out with the host and didn't come back from the wolf's front. Her bread is still on the end of your table. Nobody has moved it.
epi.skogul.rode: Skögul rode out on the last morning, as choosers do. She left you the rest of her bread, which she has never done.
epi.odin.lied: Odin never asked you about the ship again. He didn't need to. He went to the wolf with one eye and all the answers.
epi.odin.told: Odin went to the wolf knowing about the ship, because you told him. He never thanked you. From him, that's thanks.
epi.odin.led: Odin went to the wolf as the seeress said he would. On his way out he looked back once, at the gate. Skögul says he never looks back.
epi.odin.went: Odin went to the wolf as the seeress said he would, and nobody at the gate was surprised, least of all him.
epi.loki.broke: Loki's end of your table stayed empty to the end. Someone had carved two words into the wood where he used to sit: Lovely nails.
epi.loki.deal: Loki kept every name you gave him, chalked on the deck where the rail goes. He keeps things very dry.
epi.loki.detained: You stamped Loki DETAIN on the twelfth day. He sent a note from the lock-up praising the lock, and was gone by the horn. Locks are a formality, he says, like gods.
epi.loki.reported: You put Loki's name in your report. He says it's the most honest thing anyone at the gate ever did to him. He'll never forgive it, and he's delighted.
epi.loki.covered: You left Loki out of your report, and he left your family out of his. Nobody ever read either one. He finds that very funny.
epi.loki.met: The stranger with the scarred lips never did get your family's names. He asked politely, and was polite about the answer.
epi.clerk.contract: The clerk's contract came back from his department stamped DUPLICATE. He apologised for a whole day, and meant every word.
epi.clerk.helped: The man baptised twenty times for the shirts asked for a twenty-first. The clerk filed it, and sent you a copy, with thanks, in triplicate.
epi.clerk.pension: The clerk retired on his pension: a room with a window, and a table nobody else sits at. He wrote once, to say the window faces the right way.
epi.clerk.packed: The clerk packed his forms before the fire, in order, and left his end of the table cleaner than he found it.
epi.hel.sided: Hel opened her doors again the day you said the quiet dead count. Móðguðr still mentions it. Down there, that's a great deal.
epi.hel.held: Hel's gate held. Móðguðr stood on her bridge through all of it, waiting to be noticed, and at the end somebody noticed.
epi.freyja.sided: Freyja keeps a list, Skögul said. Your name is on it, near the top, in her own hand.
epi.freyja.held: Freyja's field held against the fire. She sent you a single feather from her cloak, which was either thanks or a bill.
epi.thorvald.slept: When the horn blew, Thorvald the Unlucky was asleep in a hayloft, and he slept through all of it. He's furious. He'd been looking forward to it.
epi.thorvald.home: Thorvald the Unlucky went home from your gate again, and was still alive at the end, which nobody can explain, least of all Thorvald.
epi.thorvald.sentBack: On his last visit you sent Thorvald somewhere other than home, and they sent him straight back. He says they were very nice about it. Mostly.
epi.thorvald.valhalla: You sent Thorvald the Unlucky to Valhalla on your first day, alive. He's still there, still feeling fine, and nobody on the benches has the heart to tell him.
epi.thorvald.alive: Thorvald the Unlucky is still alive. Nobody knows how, least of all Thorvald.
epi.geir.hel: Geir Hallsson's widow still leaves bread on the stone by the path, for the ones going down to Hel's hall. She says Geir would have wanted the queue fed.
epi.geir.ran: Geir Hallsson drank on Odin's benches with his broken oath still on his finger. When the wolf came he ran, first of anyone, and the skalds left him out of the song.
epi.geir.spared: Geir Hallsson drank on Odin's benches with his broken oath still on his finger. Nobody asked him about it. Nobody on Odin's benches asks anyone anything.
epi.geir.judged: Geir Hallsson went where you sent him. He sat at your father's table every winter; he'd have said you were only doing your job, and half meant it.
epi.hrolf.hel: Old Hrolf sits in Hel's hall mending nets that don't need mending. He tells everyone about the roof over the little one's bed. Tight as a drum.
epi.hrolf.judged: Old Hrolf went where you sent him. He meant to see the winter out, and nearly did.
epi.jarl.ran: Jarl Asgaut's thirty rings bought him a bench in Valhalla. When the wolf came he ran with the rest of the unworthy, and his sons put it in the song that he didn't.
epi.jarl.bench: Jarl Asgaut's thirty rings bought him a bench in Valhalla, near the door. He complains about the draught.
epi.jarl.hel: Jarl Asgaut sits in Hel's hall, telling anyone who'll listen about the thirty rings you turned down. Hel lets him. She says it passes the time.
epi.hrapp.draugr: Hrapp Oddsson still sits in his barrow up past the ford, on his silver, with the door open. The valley takes the long road round.
epi.hrapp.hel: Hrapp Oddsson sits in Hel's hall, counting her spoons. Nobody ever counted them before. She finds she likes it.
epi.carver.wrong: The carver you named drowned for another man's knife. The forged tallies kept coming until the fire, every one of them cut by a man who died in his bed.
epi.carver.right: No new tallies were cut in the valley after the carver went into the fjord. The dead came with the deeds they'd done, and for a while nobody minded.
epi.hrapp.judged: Hrapp Oddsson went where you sent him, still working out what it had cost him.
epi.svanhild.rode: Svanhild Hallvardsdottir rode out with the einherjar, eight days married and not sorry about any of it.
epi.svanhild.bench: Svanhild Hallvardsdottir sits on Odin's benches and tells anyone who'll listen about her eight days. Most of them listen.
epi.svanhild.judged: Svanhild Hallvardsdottir went where you sent her the second time, with eight good days behind her.
epi.svanhild.home: Svanhild Hallvardsdottir is alive, as far as anyone knows, and keeps well away from the ford.
epi.svanhild.alive: Svanhild Hallvardsdottir went where you sent her, still breathing, and nobody there knew what to do with her.
epi.jofrid.geir: Jofrid found Geir where you'd sent them both. She brought bread.
epi.jofrid.judged: Jofrid Arnorsdottir went where you sent her. On feast days she still bakes for a husband who isn't there.
epi.kolskegg: Kolskegg Thorkelsson never told his mother why he went up the hill. The whole valley did it for him.
epi.thorolf.father: Thorolf Asgautsson sits beside his father in Hel's hall, where nobody knows who they are. They argue about the thirty rings.
epi.thorolf.farEnd: Thorolf Asgautsson sits at the far end of Odin's benches from his father, as he asked. They nod, now and then.
epi.thorolf.bench: Thorolf Asgautsson sits on Odin's benches, and his father sits in Hel's hall among strangers.
epi.thorolf.judged: Thorolf Asgautsson went where you sent him, and didn't ask why. His father would have.
epi.gudrid: Gudrid Arnkelsdottir went where you sent her and waited for her son. He hasn't come. He never does.
epi.kari.found: Kari found his mother in Rán's hall, at a loom by the sea, and handed her the thread. On the last day they stood at the shore together.
epi.kari.searching: Kari went to Rán's hall to find his mother, but you'd sent her somewhere else. He's still looking for her along the bottom of the sea. He isn't angry, which is worse.
epi.kari.sea: Kari went to Rán's hall, to be with his mother. Bera dreamed of them both, at a loom by the sea.
epi.kari.rode: Kari rode out to the wolf with the einherjar, in the front rank, where he could see everything. Solveig would have hated it, and been proud.
epi.kari.benches: Kari sits on Odin's benches with a horn in each hand, as Bera said. Solveig would have hated it, and been proud.
epi.kari.judged: Kari went where you sent him, and didn't argue. He'd said his piece at the desk.
epi.thrand.poem: Thrand made a poem about the last battle before it was over. It's very long. You're in the ninth verse, at your table, stamping.
epi.thrand.bench: Thrand got his seat on Odin's benches. He's writing a poem about the battle before it happens, to save time.
epi.thrand.judged: Thrand never found out whether his spear mark counted. He made a poem about not knowing, and it's the best thing he ever wrote.
epi.halla.transfer: Halla, who delivered you, has a room at the clerk's end of the table. Every morning she asks him whether you're eating properly. He writes it down.
epi.halla.judged: Halla, who delivered you, went where you sent her. She'd seen you through worse, and said so on her way.
ragnarok.text: Heimdall's horn. On the plain of Vígríðr the fronts are drawn, and the hosts you filled stand waiting for you to send them. You can't be everywhere. Neither can they.
front.wolf.text: Fenrir, loose at last. His upper jaw scrapes the sky.
front.wolf.held: The wolf's front held. Odin still falls to him, as foretold, but late, and not alone.
front.wolf.fell: The wolf's front broke at the first howl. Odin fell before the horn had stopped sounding.
front.fire.text: Surtr and the sons of Muspell, coming up from the south with a sword brighter than the sun.
front.fire.held: The fire front held. Surtr's fire still came, but not everywhere, and not all at once.
front.fire.fell: The fire front fell. The fire went where it liked.
front.gate.text: Garm, the hound at the cave-mouth, off his chain and baying.
front.gate.held: Hel's gate held. Garm never got through, and the dead stayed where they were put.
front.gate.fell: Hel's gate fell. Garm ran loose, and the dead ran with him.
front.ship.text: Naglfar, the ship of dead men's nails, with Loki at the helm. Every nail you left long is one more aboard.
front.ship.held: The shore held. Rán's drowned dragged Naglfar's crew back into the sea.
front.ship.fell: The shore fell. Naglfar ran aground and Loki's crew came up the shingle.
case.thorvald16.today: Is it today? I was sure it was today.
case.thorvald16.bear: Something big trod on me in the hills last night. I never saw what.
case.thorvald16.fine: I feel fine, mostly. Is that bad?
case.hrolf.roof: Your brother mended my nets, so I helped him patch your roof.
case.hrolf.drum: Over the little one's bed. Tight as a drum now.
case.hrolf.winter: I meant to see the winter out. I nearly did.
case.solveig.frown: You're one of Ragna's. I'd know that frown anywhere.
case.solveig.herring: The herring were running. We said one more net.
case.solveig.loom: Tell them at home I left the loom threaded.
case.hallbjorn.paid: Ulf's kin? The fine's paid, I hear. The boy only carved what I drew.
case.hallbjorn.debt: Ulf's kin? Tell the jarl the boy only carved what I drew.
case.hallbjorn.real: Half the swords in the valley are mine. The better half.
case.hallbjorn.cousin: The jarl's cousin fought beside me with one of mine. It bent. He noticed.
case.thorvald9.again: You again! You sent me home last time. Nobody at home believed me.
case.thorvald9.songs: I was sure this time. They'd already started the songs.
case.thorvald9.seat: Is my seat still free? I told everyone I had a seat.
case.jarl.front: I don't stand in lines. Nobody back there minded. Ask them.
case.jarl.sons: My sons put the sword in my hand before I was cold. It's what's done, for a jarl.
case.jarl.offer: Thirty rings when that stamp says Valhalla. Odin's ring only drips eight.
case.hrapp.chest: They buried me with my chest at my feet. Seventy-one winters of saving, and I never spent a ring I didn't have to.
case.hrapp.nephews: My nephews are up at the barrow already. I can hear them digging.
case.hrapp.offer: Forty rings when that stamp says Return. I'll go back and sit on the rest. Nobody need know.
case.svanhild7.dead: They told me I was dead. I don't feel dead. I feel cold.
case.svanhild7.quiet: Is this where you come after? It's very quiet, for a hall.
case.svanhild7.father: My father's still at the ford. He'll be looking for me.
case.svanhild15.days: You sent me home last time. Eight days. I married the smith's boy, and my father saw it.
case.svanhild15.ford: Same ford. Same Danes. Different luck.
case.svanhild15.used: Don't look like that. Eight days is a long time, if you use them.
case.jofrid.bread: I brought bread to your mother's door that winter. You won't remember. You were at the gate by then.
case.jofrid.geir: Geir Hallsson was my husband. I know where you sent him. The whole valley knows.
case.jofrid.cough: It was the cough. It went through three houses, and mine was the third.
case.jofrid.plea.valhalla: {name} asks for a Valhalla stamp, to be with her husband, Geir: a mistake all the same.
case.jofrid.plea.hel: {name} asks for a Hel stamp, to be with her husband, Geir: a mistake all the same.
case.kolskegg.silver: I only went up for the silver. It wasn't doing him any good.
case.kolskegg.uncle: He was sitting on it. Uncle Hrapp. He's stronger dead than he ever was alive.
case.kolskegg.mother: Tell my mother I didn't run. Don't tell her why I went.
case.thorolf.ford: We held the ford till noon. Then I didn't, but the others did.
case.thorolf.bought: My father paid you thirty rings for his bench. He told everyone, all the way to the grave.
case.thorolf.bench: Put me at the other end of the hall from him. I'd like to earn mine.
case.thorolf.refused: My father offered you thirty rings, and you turned him down. He'll still be talking about it.
case.thorolf.strangers: He's old, and he's in Hel's hall, and nobody there knows who he is.
case.thorolf.plea: {name} asks for a Hel stamp, to sit with his father: a mistake all the same.
case.gudrid.son: I'm Thorvald's mother. He's been here, hasn't he? More than once.
case.gudrid.worry: I stopped worrying about him years ago. Well. Last winter.
case.gudrid.home: If he comes again, send him home. Somebody ought to be there.
case.kari.mother: Is this where they come from the herring? My mother went at the herring. Solveig, Arne's daughter.
case.kari.pass: We held the pass till the sun came up. Then we didn't.
case.kari.ask: I don't need Odin's benches. Send me where she is.
case.kari.plea: {name} asks for a Rán stamp, to be with his mother: a mistake all the same.
plea.hel.valhalla: {name} asks for a Valhalla stamp, to drink with {gender, select, f {her} other {his}} brothers on Odin's benches: a mistake all the same.
plea.hel.ran: {name} asks for a Rán stamp, to be with {gender, select, f {her husband} other {his wife}}, who went down with the herring boats: a mistake all the same.
plea.valhalla.hel: {name} asks for a Hel stamp, to sit with {gender, select, f {her} other {his}} mother, who died in her bed: a mistake all the same.
plea.valhalla.folkvangr: {name} asks for a Fólkvangr stamp, to be with {gender, select, f {her} other {his}} sister in Freyja's hall: a mistake all the same.
plea.ran.valhalla: {name} asks for a Valhalla stamp, to sit with the crew {gender, select, f {she} other {he}} rowed with, who fell at the ford: a mistake all the same.
plea.transfer.hel: {name} asks for a Hel stamp, to be with {gender, select, f {her} other {his}} mother and father, who were never baptized: a mistake all the same.
kin.text: {name} is {kin}'s {relation, select, wife {wife} husband {husband} other {cousin}}. You sent {kinGender, select, f {her} other {him}} to {hall, select, VALHALLA {Valhalla} FOLKVANGR {Fólkvangr} HEL {Hel's hall} RAN {Rán's hall} other {another hall}} on Day {day}, where {kinGender, select, f {she} other {he}} didn't belong.
kin.plea: {name} asks for a {dest} stamp, to be with {kinGender, select, f {her} other {him}}: a mistake all the same.
case.bard.ulf: Ulf? Planks at the next trestle. Good hands, sad face. Talks about you.
case.bard.nails: The foreman says never trim a nail. The ship needs every one.
case.bard.ship: It's a very big ship. I'm not sure it floats.
case.bjarni.list: The jarl's men came with a list of my customers. Somebody wrote letters.
case.bjarni.tally: That's my own tally. Best work I ever did.
case.bjarni.cold: Is it far, where I'm going? I've been cold since this morning.
case.bjarni.best: Best tallies on the coast. Read mine, if you like good work.
case.bjarni.hero: Families wanted heroes. I only carved what they paid for.
case.bjarni.bench: Is there a carvers' bench, where you're sending me?
case.carver.honest: Every tally I ever cut was true. Ask anyone I cut one for.
case.carver.named: They said a Valkyrie gave them my name. I've never met a Valkyrie. Have I?
case.carver.cold: The water was so cold. I kept waiting for someone to say it was a mistake.
case.thrand.spear: I had them cut me with a spear, over the heart. The way Odin did.
case.thrand.poems: All my life I made poems about battles. I never saw one.
case.thrand.count: Does it count? Tell me it counts.
case.halla.born: I delivered you, you know. You had plenty to say even then.
case.halla.promise: Your mother made me promise to look for you at the gate. Here I am.
case.halla.loaf: There was a loaf for you. They took it off me at the bridge.
tm.oath.kept.4: I swore few oaths, and I kept every one.
tm.oath.kept.5: Oaths? I kept them all. It was easier than the alternative.
tm.oath.kept.6: Ask anyone at home. I kept my word, even when it cost me.
tm.owner.self.3: My {weapon}. My name's cut into it, if you read runes.
tm.owner.self.4: This {weapon} and I go back a long way.
tm.owner.self.5: I've carried this {weapon} since I could lift it.
tm.blade.ulfberht.3: My {weapon}'s an Ulfberht. Frankish steel. You don't see many.
tm.creed.heathen.3: The midwinter sacrifice every year, like my father. The old gods, all the way.
tm.creed.heathen.4: The old gods. Is that the right answer?
tm.creed.heathen.5: I've never been near a priest. Or a river with one in it.
tm.creed.baptized.3: A priest put me in the river and said I was the White Christ's now. I took his word for it.
tm.guise.3: I'm exactly what I look like. Nothing more.
tm.guise.4: No secrets here. I never had the head for them.
tm.guise.5: Me? I'm nobody special. Just me.
tm.guise.6: I'm what I look like. Tired, mostly.
tm.identity.7: {name} {patronym}. I've stood in more shield walls than you've stamped souls.
tm.identity.8: {name} {patronym}. Is this going to take long?
tm.identity.9: I think I'm {name}. {patronym}? That sounds right.
tm.identity.10: {name} {patronym}. Ask me anything you need to.
tm.death.battle.5: We met {foe} at {place}. They had more men. That's the whole story.
tm.death.battle.6: It was {place}. The fighting went on all morning, and I didn't see it end.
tm.death.battle.7: Killed at {place}, fighting {foe}. I'd do it again, just not today.
tm.death.battle.8: {place}. Go and ask {foe} how it went. The ones still standing.
tm.death.battle.9: {foe} at {place}. Same as every summer, apart from the last part.
tm.weapon.yes.3: They'll have to prise my {weapon} out of my fist.
tm.weapon.yes.4: I had my {weapon} to the end. Still have, look.
tm.weapon.yes.5: My {weapon} and I went down together. That's how it's done.
tm.weapon.yes.6: I never let go of my {weapon}. Couldn't, by the end.
tm.back.no.3: Nobody ever saw my back in a fight.
tm.back.no.4: Nobody can say I ran. Look me over, front and back.
tm.back.no.5: I did not run. I want that written down.
tm.back.no.6: I've never shown an enemy my back, and I wasn't going to start.
tm.flavor.braggart.2: You'll want a skald for this.
tm.flavor.braggart.3: Make sure they spell my name right in the hall.
tm.flavor.confused.2: Do I keep my boots on, or is it a boots-off hall?
tm.flavor.confused.3: Somebody should feed my goats. Can you tell somebody?
tm.flavor.coward.2: Do the halls have doors? Ones that bar from the inside?
tm.flavor.coward.3: Somewhere with no fighting would suit me. Or very little.
rv.muninn.forgot.2: Muninn: I knew this one. I did. The name's gone.
rv.muninn.forgot.3: Muninn: There was a name. It was on the tip of my beak.
rv.muninn.forgot.5: Muninn: I remember the face. Only the face.
rv.muninn.forgot.6: Muninn: Something with a horse in it? I'll think of it.
rv.muninn.carved.elderRune: Muninn: This one's saga was cut over, and the first one's gone from me. The knife I remember. It likes the old rune, ᛗ.
rv.muninn.carved.mirroredRune: Muninn: Someone cut this saga again. I can't find the first. The knife cut its runes backwards, like a man copying from a pond.
rv.muninn.carved.brokenFormula: Muninn: The saga was cut over, and I've lost the first. The knife signed it "reist mik", carved me, the way a sword is signed.
rv.muninn.identity.2: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Of course I know. I'm Memory.
rv.muninn.identity.3: Muninn: That's {name} {patronym}. I never forget. Hardly ever.
rv.muninn.heathen.2: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. The old gods, every feast, every year. I remember the smoke.
rv.muninn.oathKept.2: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Said a thing, did the thing. Every time.
rv.huginn.battle.2: Huginn: Fell at {place}. I was circling. I saw.
rv.huginn.battle.3: Huginn: {place}, in the thick of it. Didn't get up.
rv.huginn.sickness.2: Huginn: A fever took this one. Slowly.
rv.huginn.oldAge.2: Huginn: Outlived everyone. Went quietly, in the night.
rv.huginn.drowned.2: Huginn: Went over the side in a squall. Didn't come up.
rv.huginn.fledTrue.2: Huginn: Ran. Fast, too. Not fast enough.
rv.huginn.fledFalse.2: Huginn: No running. Not this one. I watched.
rv.huginn.fledFalse.3: Huginn: Didn't run. I'd have seen.
rv.huginn.weapon.2: Huginn: Held on to it to the end. I watched the whole thing.
rv.huginn.weapon.3: Huginn: Never let go of it. Not once.
rv.huginn.noWeapon.2: Huginn: Nothing in the hands at the end. Nothing at all.
tl.fled.false.2: Never showed the foe their back.
tl.outlaw.false.2: Broke no oath, sworn or spoken.
thread.owesSkogul: You owe Skögul the ten rings she advanced you.
thread.ulfDebt: Ulf still owes the jarl his share of the smith's fine.
thread.ulfShipyard: Ulf is shaping planks at a shipyard in the north, for a man with very clean hands.
thread.lokiDeal: The man with the scarred lips has your family's names, and room for them on his ship.
thread.ferry: The ferryman at the mouth of the fjord is holding places for your family. He wants a hundred rings more on the day the horn blows.
thread.woodKnown: Thorvald told you of Hoddmímir's wood, where nothing can find you.
thread.wood: Your family will wait out the end in Hoddmímir's wood.
thread.stayHome: Your family will stay home when the horn blows, together.
thread.clerkContract: You've signed the clerk's contract: a table in his department when the horn blows.
thread.truth: You've heard {n, plural, one {one thing} other {# things}} about what comes after the fire.
thread.carver: Three carvers work the valley, and one of them cuts sagas over. Skögul's list is on the wall above your desk.
trail.title: The carvers
trail.intro: Three carvers cut tallies in this valley, and one of them is cutting sagas over at twelve rings a time. Every knife has its habits, and every forged tally shows one of his. What you see under the lens is pinned here; so is what Muninn remembers of a knife when he can't remember the soul. You can name one man, once, on the twelfth night or the fourteenth.
trail.bjarni: The oldest carver on the coast, and the best, if you ask him.
trail.hjalti: Cuts the jarl's memorial stones, and charges by the rune.
trail.ljot: Carves bowls and spoons as well as tallies, and never haggles.
trail.named.right: Skögul takes the name up to the hall. Before dawn the jarl's men find {name}'s knife, and a basket of new tallies under his bench. The jarl sends fifteen rings.
trail.named.wrong: Skögul takes the name up to the hall. The jarl's men find nothing in {name}'s house but bowls and honest tallies. They take him to the fjord anyway. The jarl said a name would do.
coach.d4.whim: New today: Freyja has claimed a share of the slain. Her whim for today is at the top of the rules: read it.
coach.d4.look: Now look for her whim on this soul.
coach.d4.stamp: Worthy, and just what Freyja asked for: she takes them. Stamp FÓLKVANGR, not VALHALLA.
coach.d5.lips: New today: the sea. Look at the lips.
coach.d5.stamp: Sea-foam on the lips: the sea took this one, and the drowned belong to Rán. Stamp RÁN.
coach.d6.registry: New today: the registry of outlaws and oathbreakers. Look this soul up in it.
coach.d6.stamp: Their name is in it. Outlaws and oathbreakers go to Hel, however well they died. Stamp HEL.
coach.d7.lens: New today: the rune-lens. A weapon carries its owner's name. Read this one's.
coach.d7.owner: The name on the blade isn't theirs: they borrowed it. Only a warrior's own weapon counts.
coach.d7.stamp: Whoever fell with someone else's weapon goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
coach.d8.nails: New today: Naglfar is built from dead men's nails. Look at the hands.
coach.d8.clip: Nails left long go to the ship. Clip them before you send the soul on.
coach.d8.stamp: Clipped. The clippers don't change where a soul goes: judge this one as you would have.
coach.d10.neck: New today: the clerk of the White Christ. Look at what this soul wears at the neck.
coach.d10.stamp: A cross alone: baptized, so the clerk takes them. Stamp TRANSFER. A hammer beside the cross means only prime-signed, and they stay yours.
coach.d11.tally: This soul brought a saga tally. Read it.
coach.d11.lens: New today: forgers. Hold the rune-lens over the tally: a forger gets a rune wrong.
coach.d11.stamp: Forged. A forged tally counts for nothing: judge by the body alone.
coach.d12.lips: New today: Loki walks among the dead. Look closely at the lips.
coach.d12.stamp: Scars where the lips were sewn: the dwarf Brokkr sewed Loki's mouth shut. Whoever he says he is, stamp DETAIN.
coach.d13.ravens: New today: both ravens speak. Huginn saw how they died; Muninn remembers how they lived. Read them.
coach.d13.stamp: The ravens never lie, but they can seem to disagree. When they do, the Order of Judgment decides: the first rule that fits wins.
coach.d14.rules: New today: Hel's hall is full. Until she has room, those who died in their beds go to the clerk.
coach.d14.skin: How did this one die? Look at the skin.
coach.d14.stamp: Sickness or old age, and nothing earlier in the Order claims them: stamp TRANSFER, not HEL.
coach.d15.claims: New today: Odin names his own claim each day, as Freyja does. Both are at the top of the rules.
coach.d15.stamp: This soul fits both. When Odin and Freyja both want a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins. Stamp VALHALLA.
coach.d16.catch: New today: a worthy soul caught lying forfeits the hall. This one lies. Catch it: tap what they say, then what shows it false.
coach.d16.stamp: Caught. The halls of the worthy won't take a liar. Stamp HEL.
coach.d17.chest: New today: Odin's mark. Look over the heart.
coach.d17.stamp: A spear's cut, made before death: they were marked for Odin, and the marked go to Valhalla, even from their beds. Stamp VALHALLA.
twist.freyja: Freyja is greedy this round: her whim fits more of the worthy than usual.
twist.sea: A fleet went down in the night. The sea gives up its dead.
twist.forgers: The carvers have been busy. More souls than usual bring saga tallies, and not every tally is honest.
twist.loki: Loki has brought friends. Watch the lips.
twist.muninn: Muninn is tired. He forgets more than he remembers this round.
ach.odin.text: Keep Odin's hall full to the end, and be named chooser for the world after.
ach.freyja.text: Give Freyja the souls she asked for, and be taken in among her own.
ach.hel.text: Fill the quiet hall, and be made its steward.
ach.naglfar.text: Leave the nails long, take Loki's bargain, and sail early.
ach.transfer.text: Sign the clerk's contract and take the warmer room.
ach.smuggled.text: Pay the ferryman to take your family where the wolf can't follow.
ach.rebirth.text: Learn what Odin knew, and walk your family out onto the green earth.
ach.wolf.text: Watch the fire come from the gate.
ach.lastStand.text: Judge all twenty days, and see the host you chose fight and fall.
ach.stitched.title: Stitched
ach.unlucky.title: Unlucky, not dead
ach.unlucky.text: Send Thorvald the Unlucky home the first time he comes, and the last.
ach.nobodyLeft.title: Nobody left behind
ach.nobodyLeft.text: Reach Ragnarök with your whole family still at home.
ach.everyFront.title: Every front held
ach.everyFront.text: At Ragnarök, hold the wolf, the fire, Hel's gate and the shore.
ach.spotless.title: Spotless
ach.spotless.text: Judge every soul rightly on a campaign day, Day 10 or later.
ach.thrice.title: Thrice cursed
ach.thrice.text: Score 100 in one Endless run with three curses on it.
ach.oathkept.title: Oathsworn
ach.oathkept.text: Reach the last day under the oath: no hints, no replays, and fines from the first mistake.
ach.carver.title: The knife's habits
ach.carver.text: Name the carver who forged the tallies.
weave.sea.text: This run is woven otherwise. Rán's rule is read before the registry's and the clerk's: the drowned are hers, even outlaws, even the baptized.
weave.clerkLast.text: This run is woven otherwise. The clerk's rule is read after every hall's but Hel's: the baptized are his only when no other rule claims them.
weave.freyjaFirst.text: This run is woven otherwise. Freyja's rule is read before Odin's claim: when both want the same worthy soul, hers wins.
event.storm.text: A storm came in off the sea in the night. The drowned are coming up with the tide, and the clouds are taking the light early.
event.sickness.text: A coughing sickness is going round the valley. More who died in their beds are waiting at the gate, and tonight it may reach your house, whatever you pay for.
event.battle.text: Two jarls met at the ford at dawn. The line is longer today, and the sun keeps a while longer to judge them by.
event.feast.text: The jarl is holding a feast, and the fighting has stopped for it. Fewer souls come to the gate today, and tonight your family eats at his hall.
event.frost.text: A hard frost came down in the night and stayed. The sun barely clears the ridge today, and tonight the hearth at home eats half as much wood again.
event.outlaws.text: The jarl's men went up into the hills after the outlaws who've been taking sheep. Three of the hunted are in your line today, their names still in the registry.
boon.shield.name: Skögul's shield
boon.shield.text: One more wrong stamp before the run ends.
boon.mending.name: Eir's mending
boon.mending.text: The healer looks over your record and tuts. One more wrong stamp before the run ends.
boon.eye.name: Skögul's eye
boon.eye.text: Three of Skögul's hints, for any round: she points at what decides a soul.
boon.bounty.name: Odin's bounty
boon.bounty.text: A soul you catch in a lie before the stamp scores 1 more.
boon.tongues.name: Loose tongues
boon.tongues.text: Every soul can be pressed once more.
boon.linger.name: Sól lingers
boon.linger.text: A minute more sun each round.
boon.hands.name: Quick hands
boon.hands.text: Turning a body over and the tools cost half the sun.
boon.bragi.name: Bragi's ear
boon.bragi.text: The first two questions each round cost no sun.
curse.sun.name: The sun rises
curse.sun.text: From now on every round has a sun, at its day's own pace. Souls still in line at dusk score nothing.
curse.hel.name: Hel's impatience
curse.hel.text: One wrong stamp fewer before the run ends.
curse.tyr.name: Týr's oath
curse.tyr.text: Swear to accuse no one lightly: a Compare that finds nothing is a strike.
curse.hurry.name: Sköll at her heels
curse.hurry.text: The wolf chases the sun harder. A quarter of each round's sun is gone.
curse.heavy.name: Heavy hands
curse.heavy.text: Turning a body over and the tools cost double the sun.
party.fight.title: Fell together at {place}
party.crew.title: The crew of the {ship}
rule.retinue: A hearth-man who stood by his jarl to the end, and never fled, goes where his jarl goes. Stamp his jarl's hall.
party.retinue.title: Jarl {lord} and {lgender, select, f {her} other {his}} hearth-men
pl.ret.lord.fled.false.1: Jarl {companion} never turned {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} back at {place}. We were right behind {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}}. We'd have seen.
pl.ret.lord.fled.false.2: {companion} ran from no one at {place}. Not from {foe}, not from anyone. Put that first, whatever you're writing.
pl.ret.lord.fled.true.1: Jarl {companion} ran when {foe} broke through at {place}. We stayed. Somebody had to.
pl.ret.lord.fled.true.2: Was it the jarl who ran first at {place}? I think it was. I think it was {companion}.
pl.ret.sworn.fled.false.1: {companion} stood by me to the end at {place}. Every one of my hearth-men did.
pl.ret.sworn.fled.false.2: {companion}? Held beside me at {place} to the last. I choose my men well.
pl.ret.sworn.fled.true.1: {companion} swore on my ring, and ran at {place}. I saw {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} back going.
pl.fled.false.1: {companion} stood beside me at {place}. Never turned {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} back. Not once.
pl.fled.false.2: {companion} held the line at {place} with the best of them. Never ran. Write that down.
pl.fled.true.1: {companion}? Ran, the moment {foe} came over the rise at {place}. I saw {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} back all the way down the hill.
pl.fled.true.2: Ask {companion} which way {cgender, select, f {she} other {he}} was facing at {place}. Away. Running.
pl.grip.weapon.1: {companion} had {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} weapon in hand to the end. I saw it.
pl.grip.weapon.2: {companion} never let go of {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} weapon. They'll have to prise it out.
pl.grip.none.1: {companion} lost {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} weapon early. Died empty-handed.
pl.grip.none.2: {companion} dropped {cgender, select, f {her} other {his}} weapon the first time anyone swung at {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}}. Embarrassing, really.
pl.cause.drowned.1: {companion} went down with the {ship} off {place}. The sea took {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}} and never gave {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}} back.
pl.cause.drowned.2: {companion} went into the water with the {ship}. Or was that someone else? No. It was {companion}.
pl.cause.battle.1: {companion} was cut down on the deck of the {ship}, before she ever sank.
pl.cause.battle.2: {foe} boarded the {ship} off {place}. {companion} took three of them with {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}} before the fourth.
pl.cause.sickness.1: {companion} was sick the whole voyage. Fever. {cgender, select, f {She} other {He}} was gone before the {ship} went down.
pl.cause.oldAge.1: {companion}? Old as the {ship}'s keel. Died at the oars, peaceful as you like.
q.party.confess.1: …Fine. What I said of {companion} wasn't so. I don't know why I said it.
q.party.fled.cover.confess.1: …All right. {companion} ran. I only wanted {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}} beside me in the good hall.
q.party.fled.spite.confess.1: …No. {companion} held. I just never liked {cgender, select, f {her} other {him}}.
q.party.grip.cover.confess.1: {cgender, select, f {Her} other {His}} hand was empty. I thought if I said it enough, it wouldn't be.
q.party.grip.spite.confess.1: …{companion} kept hold of it. {cgender, select, f {She} other {He}} owed me a cow.
q.party.cause.confess.1: …That isn't how {companion} died. I wanted us in the same hall, that's all.
q.party.excuse.1: It was a battle. Everyone looks like everyone else from behind.
q.party.coward.excuse.1: I wasn't really looking at {companion}. I was looking for the way out.
